\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Boolean function over the two-element field]
\lean{FABL.booleanFunctionF₂Encoding}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binarySignEquiv}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p019-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p169-b008
}
For a function $f$ from the $n$-dimensional sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to $\\{\\pm1\\}$,
define its two-element-field encoding on $\\mathbb F_2^n$ by identifying each input sign
vector with its binary vector and each output sign with its corresponding element of
$\\mathbb F_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Real indicator of a Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.booleanRealEmbedding}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p022-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p150-b001
}
\label{FABL.booleanRealEmbedding}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.PseudoBooleanFunction}
For a function $f:\\mathbb F_2^n\\to\\mathbb F_2$, define a real-valued function on
$\\mathbb F_2^n$ that equals $1$ where $f(x)=1$ and equals $0$ everywhere else.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sign encoding of a Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.signEncode_booleanFunctionF₂Encoding}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binarySignEquiv, FABL.booleanFunctionF₂Encoding, FABL.signEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let
$x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The sign encoding of the value of the binary encoding of $f$ at
$x$ equals $f$ evaluated at the sign vector corresponding to $x$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.booleanRealEmbedding}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p143-b004}
\proofstep
  {FABL.PseudoBooleanFunction}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p143-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b003}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $x$ be a vector in the $n$-dimensional cube over the
field with two elements. The real-valued embedding of the binary encoding of $f$,
evaluated at $x$, equals one half of $1$ minus the real value of $f$ at the
corresponding sign vector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Boolean embedding in sign coordinates]

  {FABL.PseudoBooleanFunction}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b003}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a function from the sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$
to $\\{-1,1\\}$. Encode its inputs as binary vectors and its outputs as elements of
$\\mathbb{F}_2$, then map an output to $1$ if it is $1$ and to $0$ otherwise. When
expressed back on the sign cube, the resulting real-valued function at $x$ is
$(1-f(x))/2$.
\end{theorem}
